title: Withdrawal and Refiling under the Member Appeals Program
content:
**Rule.**

- When the member's Northbridge Appeals package allows withdrawal, the appellant may withdraw an appeal under the Member Appeals Program that has not yet been decided.
- A withdrawn appeal takes no decision.
- When the package allows refiling, a withdrawn appeal may be refiled while the original filing limit has not passed.
- An appeal may be withdrawn only when it has no decision and no earlier withdrawal.

## Questions answered

**Who may withdraw an appeal?** The appellant.

**Can an appeal that has already been upheld or overturned be withdrawn?** No. An appeal may be withdrawn only while it has no decision.

**Can an appeal be withdrawn twice?** No. An appeal that already has a withdrawal cannot be withdrawn again.

**What happens to a withdrawn appeal?** It takes no decision: it is neither upheld nor overturned.

**Can the matter be appealed again after a withdrawal?** Yes, when the package allows refiling, but only while the original filing limit has not passed. That limit is the same one that applied to the appeal before it was withdrawn, counted from the same date. Withdrawing does not restart it.

## Worked case (hypothetical dates)

A member appeals a denial whose notice was dated 1 March and withdraws the appeal on 20 April, before any decision.

- The withdrawal is allowed, because the appeal had no decision and had not been withdrawn before.
- The appeal takes no decision.
- The member may refile on any day up to the last day of the original filing limit counted from 1 March, when the package allows refiling.
